output.title: Timezone handling usually hides a workflow decision
output.body:
Timezone handling looks like a small annoyance, but it often hides a repeatable workflow problem: replies land late, follow-ups slip, and someone ends up reading timestamps by hand more than once. The trap is to treat that as a simple conversion issue. In a small business, it is usually a routing problem in disguise.

The bounded decision is not whether to automate everything. It is whether to automate one timezone-aware path: incoming email, task reminders, or logged requests. That is narrower than a CRM rebuild, and easier to judge honestly. If the same confusion only appears once in a while, manual rules may be enough. If it keeps coming back, you may have a real workflow candidate.

Keep the decision with the owner. Software can flag the sender’s timezone, normalize timestamps, or suggest a sensible follow-up window, but the owner decides what gets deferred, what gets escalated, and what counts as too late. Time-sensitive work is not a place to let a tool wander off on its own.

A practical next step is simple: log one week of timezone-related friction. Note what repeated, where it came from, and whether it needed a human decision. If the list is mostly edge cases, stay manual. If the same pattern keeps reappearing, you have something bounded enough to discuss.

This is not glamorous work. That is usually the point.
